Single–particle levels in a one–dimensional infinite square-well have energies  

 εn = n²E , n = 1,2,3,… ,  with  E = π²ħ² /(2mL²).

Because the four particles are identical spin-½ fermions, the Pauli principle allows at most two particles (one spin-up, one spin-down) in any spatial level n.

Ground state  
• Fill the lowest available spatial levels, two particles per level:  
 n = 1 : 2 particles → energy 2·1²E = 2E  
 n = 2 : 2 particles → energy 2·2²E = 8E  
Total ground–state energy: E₀ = 2E + 8E = 10E

First excited state  
The smallest possible excitation is to move one of the particles in n = 2 up to the next empty level n = 3:  
 ΔE = (3² – 2²)E = (9 – 4)E = 5E  
 E₁ = 10E + 5E = 15E

Second excited state  
Next‐higher energy is obtained by instead moving one of the n = 1 particles to n = 3 (all other lower excitations already counted):  
 ΔE = (3² – 1²)E = (9 – 1)E = 8E  
 E₂ = 10E + 8E = 18E

(Other possibilities give larger totals: 20E, 22E, 23E, …)

Thus

Ground state energy = 10E  
First excited state   = 15E  
Second excited state = 18E

Matching the listed possibilities, this corresponds to option (D).

Answer: D
